videos.title: Polska największym przegranym wojny na Ukrainie. Kto na niej zarabia? | Sykulski, Kalbarczyk
videos.description:
Polska wydała na wojnę za wschodnią granicą prawie pół biliona złotych, a przy stole w Abu Zabi nie było nikogo z Warszawy. Leszek Sykulski i Artur Kalbarczyk rozkładają na części, kto na tej wojnie zarabia, kto za nią płaci i co oznacza krach, który właśnie przetacza się przez giełdy.

Rozmawiamy o Putinie z walizką nuklearną, o statku zniszczonym dronami na Bałtyku i o tym, czy ukraińskie drony mogą latać nad Polską. Pytamy, czy prezydent powinien jechać do Moskwy i po co Europie koalicja chętnych. Potem schodzimy na ziemię: syreny o siódmej rano pod szkołą na Lubelszczyźnie, pomysł odebrania obywatelom broni, limity gotówki i pieniądz cyfrowy z datą ważności. videos.title: Les Gets: tłumy, dziury i łatwe trasy. Dla kogo jest najsłynniejszy bikepark Francji?
videos.description:
Ubezpieczenie dla rowerzystów
https://sportowcy-phi.pl/?partnerId=dirtit

Les Gets w Portes du Soleil uchodzi za najbardziej znany francuski bike park. To trzeci przystanek naszego trzeciego tripa i miejsce, które po hardcore'owej Szwajcarii i freeride'owym Châtel ma opinię najbardziej familijnego w regionie. Sprawdzam, czy poza łagodnymi trasami znajdzie się tu coś dla bardziej zaawansowanych riderów.

32 bikeparki, 4 tripy, jeden sezon.

Bike park opiera się na trzech wyciągach i ponad 10 trasach, z których większość jest naprawdę łatwa. Nawet czerwone są tu wyraźnie łagodniejsze niż w Châtel. Podczas naszego pobytu, po suchym lecie i przy takich tłumach, wiele tras było mocno rozbitych, choć widać, że są na bieżąco poprawiane.

Magda jedzie ze mną niebieskie The Shore i 888 Lower Section. Tutejsze podłoże podoba się jej bardziej niż w Châtel: mniej kamieni, więcej ziemi i mimo niedawnych burz praktycznie bez błota. Same niebieskie trasy wydały się jej jednak trochę nijakie. Na najłagodniejszym zjeździe Magda mogła się rozpędzić i dobrze bawić, a ja się nudziłem. To dobrze pokazuje, dla kogo jest ta część Les Gets.

Ciekawiej robi się dla mnie na ProLine, pomarańczowej trasie z oznaczeniem double diamond, do której podchodzę kilka razy. Na koniec dnia jadę on sight czarny Le Canyon i przejeżdżam na Mont Chéry, żeby pierwszy raz zobaczyć trasę Oakley z dropami i wallride'em.

Mówię też szczerze o zmęczeniu. Trzeci trip, praca przed świtem i jeszcze po jeździe: to fajny projekt, ale nie wakacje.

Les Gets to bardzo familijny bike park z rozbudowaną infrastrukturą i dużym atutem całego Portes du Soleil: doliny, bike parki, a nawet kraje są tu połączone trasami i wyciągami. Dla początkujących i rodzin to dobre miejsce. Bardziej zaawansowani znajdą kilka fajnych hop, ale przy dziurach i tłumach nie mam tu zajawki, żeby jeździć góra-dół.

Napiszcie w komentarzu, czy pojechalibyście tyle kilometrów, żeby pojeździć we Francji.

videos.title: The Psychology of People Who Sabotage Their Own Success
videos.description:
Why do you sabotage yourself right before success? There's a name for it in psychology: self-handicapping. It's 3 a.m., your big interview is in six hours, and you're reorganizing your sock drawer.

You know you should be asleep, and you don't stop. The next day it doesn't go well, and a quiet voice says something strangely comforting: "Well, I didn't really prepare."

That voice isn't laziness. In 1978 at Duke University, Steven Berglas and Edward Jones offered students two pills before a test. One, they were told, would help them perform better. The other would make them perform worse. And many of the students who had succeeded without understanding why chose the bad one. That is self-handicapping: buying an excuse in advance. This video follows it through three reasons we build a back door before the things we care about most, and what actually helps you close it.

videos.title: 10 000 kroków, 8 godzin snu. Status: wykonane
videos.description:
Christina Draganich udowodniła: fałszywy wynik snu zmienia myślenie. 164 osoby, 62 punkty i 8 godzin snu jako egzamin.

Odcinek wyjaśnia, jak trackery snu i zegarki zamieniają odpoczynek w zadanie z oceną. To materiał dla każdego, kto rano sprawdza wynik regeneracji, liczy kroki i celuje w 10 000 kroków dziennie. Główna teza brzmi: pomiar pokazuje zmiany, lecz dopiero ocena każe nam zasypiać na punkty.

Christina Draganich i Kristi Erdal podały 164 osobom zmyślone wyniki: 28,7% albo 16,2% fazy REM. Uczestnicy przekonani o dobrym śnie lepiej wypadli w części testów uwagi i myślenia. Fałszywa ocena nie zmieniła nocy, lecz zmieniła przekonanie o własnej formie następnego dnia.

W 2025 roku badacze porównali 6 urządzeń z polisomnografią u 62 osób. Trackery trafnie wykryły ponad 90% snu, lecz czuwanie rozpoznały słabo. Lekarze już w 2017 roku opisali ortosomnię, czyli pogoń za idealnym snem z aplikacji, a badanie z 2024 roku na 523 osobach dało 3, 8,6 i 14%.

Krótka przerwa między zmianami nie daje snu: 11 godzin przerwy to za mało, gdy doliczyć dojazdy i dom. Na 66 oddziałach norweskiego szpitala ograniczenie krótkich przerw poprawiło część wskaźników snu. Eurofound w 2023 roku dodał drugą połowę obrazu: ponad 80% ankietowanych dostaje służbowe wiadomości po godzinach.

Wniosek dotyczy wolności, nie wyniku: zegarek zauważy krótszą noc, lecz spokoju nie zapewni. Odpoczynek wymaga rozpoznania własnych potrzeb oraz warunków, które pozwalają zgodnie z nimi postępować. Prawdziwy odpoczynek nie wymaga oceny i zaczyna się tam, gdzie kończy się poprawianie siebie.

Jimmy interviews investment banker and former HUD official Katherine Austin Fitts about central bank digital currencies and the possibility that digital financial systems could eliminate privacy and give authorities greater control over individual transactions. Austin-Fitts describes an “automatic third lock,” in which surveillance infrastructure and algorithms could freeze accounts, block payments, or impose financial penalties without the human review and appeal processes available in current banking systems. 

She urges people to preserve access to cash and supports state-level legislation to resist financial centralization, while warning that a transition to an all-digital system could cause serious harm. videos.title: Why Are Mountain Bikers Running Their Stems BACKWARDS?
videos.description:
Mountain bike cockpits are getting weird. Really weird.

We've been seeing a growing trend toward super-short stems and ridiculously high-rise handlebars, with some riders even flipping their stems around to achieve negative reach. So naturally, we had to give it a try.

We're running the Hope 20mm Gravity Stem paired with 50mm-rise Burgtec handlebars to create one seriously unusual MTB cockpit. Flip the stem around and things get even stranger, bringing your hands closer to the rider with negative effective stem length.

But is there actually something to this setup, or is it just another weird mountain bike trend? We take it out on the trails to find out.

Would you try this cockpit setup? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: Mutual Fund Overlap Myth Busted! Does Investing in Multiple Funds Hurt Returns? | Revanth Chalamala
videos.description:
Are you holding multiple mutual funds from the same category? Is mutual fund portfolio overlap really a problem? Many investors believe that investing in multiple Flexi Cap, Multi Cap or Small Cap funds leads to unnecessary stock overlap and reduces returns. But is this actually true?

In this detailed data-driven analysis, Revanth Chalamala busts one of the biggest myths in mutual fund investing using **2,286 mutual fund combinations** across Flexi Cap, Multi Cap and Small Cap categories.

We analyse real portfolio data to understand whether stock overlap affects mutual fund returns and why simply counting common stocks can give misleading results.

**What you will learn in this video:**

- Is investing in multiple mutual funds from the same category wrong?
- Does having 15–20 mutual funds create unnecessary portfolio overlap?
- What is mutual fund portfolio overlap?
- Why stock overlap percentage alone is misleading.
- How to calculate portfolio overlap using stock weightage.
- Number of common stocks vs weight-based overlap.
- How fund allocation and stock weightages impact returns.
- Flexi Cap vs Flexi Cap overlap analysis.
- Multi Cap vs Multi Cap overlap analysis.
- Small Cap vs Small Cap overlap analysis.
- Does high portfolio overlap necessarily mean similar returns?
- Why two funds holding the same stocks can generate different returns.
- The importance of fund manager conviction, investment philosophy and strategy.
- Growth vs Value vs Momentum vs Quality investing strategies.

We tested 2,286 fund combinations and analysed portfolio overlap at different levels to understand its actual impact on returns. The findings challenge the common belief that having multiple mutual funds or overlapping stocks is automatically a bad investment decision.

The biggest takeaway: Don't select mutual funds just by looking at stock overlap percentages. Understand the fund manager's investment philosophy, portfolio allocation, strategy and consistency before making investment decisions.

videos.title: What Will Happen to America's $40 Trillion Debt in the Next 10 Years?
videos.description:
America's Debt in 2036: Who Pays the Price?

America's national debt has already passed $40 trillion, and the Congressional Budget Office projects that debt held by the public could reach about $56 trillion by 2036, with net interest costs of roughly $2.1 trillion a year. The danger isn't a sudden bankruptcy. It's a slow squeeze: higher borrowing costs, slower growth, an aging population, harder budget choices, and less room to respond to the next crisis. We look at how big the debt really is, how America got here, the interest trap, what it means for mortgages and businesses, why the U.S. can't simply print its way out, the Federal Reserve's balancing act, the dollar's global role, and three possible paths to 2036.

videos.title: Do BRICS Even Need a Common Currency?
videos.description:
Do BRICS Even Need a Common Currency? Discover why the viral dedollarization headlines miss how money, economics, and international finance actually function across emerging financial markets today.

In this video from Think BRICS, we break down the reality behind the proposed brics currency and brics common currency debates dominating recent BRICS news. Beyond dramatic headlines from each annual brics summit, global trade relies on functional bilateral mechanics rather than overnight monetary unions. We examine how member economies—including Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa—navigate foreign policy priorities, international relations, and trade imbalances while moving away from the us dollar.

Instead of printing a single physical banknote or establishing a unified central bank, member states are building practical alternatives to safeguard cross-border commerce: • Bilateral currency settlement mechanisms (such as India-Russia energy trades settled in national rupees) • The expanding lending operations of the New Development Bank (the BRICS Bank) • Alternative cross-border messaging infrastructure and the emerging BRICS Payment System • Strategies deployed by the global majority to insulate sovereign assets against unilateral freezes

Through pragmatic analysis of macroeconomics, capital accounts, and liquidity constraints, we explain how the russia china brics axis and the wider multipolar world seek financial independence from western clearing corridors without creating an unworkable common currency.

To keep this analysis clear and grounded in financial reality, this breakdown does not cover speculative cryptocurrency schemes, sensational predictions claiming the dollar collapses overnight, or unverified rumors regarding a physical gold-backed retail paper note. It does not provide personal financial markets advice, trading tips, or speculative investment strategies for foreign exchange holdings. Furthermore, this video avoids abstract treaty speculation, focusing strictly on functional economics, central bank settlement flows, and observable developments shaping the changing world order.

videos.title: I Nearly Destroyed Myself Here! | Crazy Steep MTB Trails
videos.description:
18 months ago and the crash - https://youtu.be/3GHg3zjxW6s?is=rE4xDUC9mgntNgHw

This time we're heading into the wild trails of Dent and Lowther Park in Cumbria, home to some seriously steep, technical and challenging natural mountain biking terrain!

It's been around 18 months since I suffered one of my biggest and scariest MTB crashes on Dent, going straight over the handlebars on a particularly nasty section of trail. I was incredibly lucky to walk away in one piece!

Now we're back exploring these incredible trails, tackling steep descents, rocky sections, tight technical corners and some properly demanding natural terrain.

Dent and Lowther Park offer a fantastic mix of challenging mountain biking, stunning Cumbrian scenery and trails that really test your confidence, bike handling and ability to pick the right lines. This is proper natural MTB riding at its finest!

⚠️ IMPORTANT SAFETY WARNING

These are extremely steep and technical trails and should only be attempted by confident, experienced mountain bikers with the appropriate skills and equipment. Some sections have serious consequences if you get things wrong, as I found out the hard way!

Always ride within your limits, inspect unfamiliar features and don't be afraid to get off and walk sections you're not comfortable with. No trail is worth a serious injury.

If you enjoy natural mountain biking, technical descents, Lake District adventures and a bit of carnage along the way, you're in the right place!

videos.title: Why Ryan Gilchrist Skipped Races to Win the World Championship

It worked.

Fresh from winning the 2026 UCI Enduro World Championships in Finale Ligure, Ryan joins Chris to reveal how four weeks of focused preparation helped deliver the rainbow jersey.

We get into his aggressive opening stage, the pressure of leading, his battle with Elliot Jamieson and Yeti teammate Richie Rude, and the strategy behind his World Championship victory.

Ryan also reflects on a huge season that included his third consecutive King of Crankworx title, his first Elite Enduro World Cup victory, Red Bull Hardline, a mid-season bike change and the physical cost of an incredibly demanding race calendar.

Plus, with the future of professional enduro uncertain, could racing less actually make him faster?

videos.title: Grenoside and Wharncliffe Woods: The BEST MTB Day Out
videos.description:
Grenoside and Wharncliffe Woods sit right next door to each other on the edge of Sheffield, and they couldn't ride more differently. One is pump track style flow with jumps and berms galore, the other is rocky, slippy, janky tech. Put them together and you get one of the best mountain biking days out in the UK.

In this video we start at Grenoside, lapping the DH track with the gang. It's the ultimate pump track like flow on a mountain bike, with fast sections, jumps and berms back to back. Simply put, the best time on two wheels.

Next we move over to DH3, also on offer here, which has a few more big jump features and a long flow track that's perfect for progressing your riding.

I got the drone out for a mini edit, and we even hit the black gap jump line. It ended with one of the boys getting bucked and nose diving into the landing, so don't say we didn't warn you!

Then comes the complete switch up at Wharncliffe. We went straight into Varsity, a slippy, loose and rocky tech track that eventually opens up into a rapid, leaf covered trail towards the bottom. It's the perfect introduction to the different style of riding Wharny has to offer.

After that we headed to Side Slab, another techy trail packed with rock drops, rock gardens and rock slabs that will scare any mountain biker. It was a great test of our skills on terrain I'm certainly not used to.

The real fun comes at the Deepcar end, where hand built tracks all start from the same point, offering jumps, flow, tech and berms galore. We hit Rake & Bake, Thora & Alec, Smile & Wave and Brown Dot, and it was some of the best riding I've had in months. I honestly don't know why I don't visit more often.

Whether you're after pump track flow, big jumps or proper rocky tech, Grenoside and Wharncliffe Woods are well worth the trip for any mountain biker visiting Sheffield!

videos.title: Cautiously Bullish On AI -- Podcast with Apollo's Brilliant Chief Economist Torsten Slok
videos.description:
This is Torsten's fourth Economics Matters podcast. As you'll agree, it's a sober discussion of AI with Torsten expressing, on balance, much more optimism than me. But facts are hard things and Torsten is the world's top producer, discoverer, and distiller of macroeconomic facts. In this podcast, Torsten shares the AI facts. As you'll see/hear, AI is not just a big deal. It's essentially the only deal driving U.S. economic growth and national wealth in recent years, measured both in terms of GDP growth, via AI's contribution to investment, and the rise in the stock market. AI is on track to account for more than half of total US net domestic investment by 2028 and two thirds by 2030. That's putting lots of our investment eggs in the one basket. Torsten, although cautiously optimistic, acknowledges that AI will need to deliver major productivity gains to justify its past let alone future spending. He also makes clear that there is no sign, to date, that AI is impacting aggregate US labor productivity or, indeed, employment. We also discussed the possibility for AI to dramatically raise productivity, but not produce profits sufficient to justify its investment. That would böse ended (end badly, as the Germans put it) for U.S. stockholders, but be a great thing for the country unless, of course, a stock market plunge puts the economy in recession, which has so often been the case. 

Torsten is Partner and Chief Economist at Apollo. Prior to joining in 2020, Torsten worked for 15 years on the sell-side, where his team was top-ranked by Institutional Investor in fixed income and equities for ten years. Previously, he worked at the OECD in Paris in the Money and Finance Division and the Structural Policy Analysis Division. Before joining the OECD, Torsten was with the IMF in the division responsible for writing the World Economic Outlook, and the division responsible for China, Hong Kong, and Mongolia.
Torsten studied at University of Copenhagen and Princeton University. He frequently appears in the media and has published numerous journal articles and reviews on economics and policy analysis, including in the Journal of International Economics, Journal of International Money and Finance, and The Econometric Journal.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

videos.title: Bitcoin, XRP i Solana ‼️ Przepowiednie się spełniły @ConstantineCrypto
videos.description:
#bitcoin #solana #xrp 
Krótkoterminowa sytuacja bitcoin dzisiaj pokazuje, czy rynek utrzymuje wcześniejsze tempo, czy zaczyna przechodzić w spokojniejszą fazę. W dłuższym horyzoncie bitcoin przyszlosc zależy między innymi od adopcji, płynności i warunków makroekonomicznych. Szerokie bitcoin informacje pozwalają łączyć ruch ceny z wiadomościami i zmianami nastrojów inwestorów. Materiały bitcoin polski ułatwiają lokalnym użytkownikom śledzenie globalnych wydarzeń bez bariery językowej. Najnowsze bitcoin aktualnosci mogą szybko wpływać na oczekiwania i zmienność. Dlatego bitcoin prognoza powinna być regularnie porównywana z rzeczywistą strukturą rynku.

Nowa solana aktualizacja może pokazać, czy w sieci pojawiły się ważne zmiany techniczne lub wzrost aktywności użytkowników. Obserwując solana dzisiaj, można ocenić krótkoterminowy impet i reakcję rynku na ostatnie wydarzenia. Pytanie solana co dalej warto rozpatrywać zarówno od strony technicznej, jak i fundamentalnej. Solana wykres pozwala zobaczyć, gdzie znajdują się istotne strefy wsparcia i oporu. Dla osób szukających treści po polsku solana polski może ułatwić zrozumienie bardziej złożonych zmian w ekosystemie. Różne solana prognoza pokazują, jak odmienne scenariusze mogą powstać przy silnym, neutralnym lub słabszym rynku.

Aktualna xrp cena pokazuje, jak inwestorzy wyceniają najnowsze wydarzenia związane z XRP. Poprzez xrp wykres można ocenić, czy obecny ruch znajduje potwierdzenie w poprzednich poziomach technicznych. Pytanie xrp co dalej staje się szczególnie istotne, gdy rynek zbliża się do ważnych stref. Nowe xrp ripple wiadomości mogą zmienić sentyment, zwłaszcza jeśli dotyczą regulacji, płatności lub adopcji. Różne xrp prognozy warto porównywać z rzeczywistym zachowaniem ceny zamiast traktować je jako pewny wynik. Dla lokalnych odbiorców xrp polska może pomóc śledzić najważniejsze wydarzenia w bardziej zrozumiałej formie.

Zayd Awan's dissertation was submitted to the New School of Psychotherapy and Counseling
and the Psychology Department of Middlesex University, in partial fulfillment of
the requirements for the Degree of Doctorate of Existential Psychotherapy and Counsel ling by Professional Studies (DProf).

This research is the first in depth participant study of the lived experience of creativity in the context of the embodied thinking practice Thinking at the Edge (TAE). The primary aim of the research is to investigate an opening and possible bridge from the novel experiences of creativity reported around TAE and into psychotherapeutic practice. Eight TAE trainees participated in this study.

To delve into this embodied practice and develop new concepts and meanings from the experience of participants, the phenomenological methodological approach of Les Todres Embodied Inquiry was used in conjunction with adjustments from the method of Micro phenomenology. The data was collected using a 90 minute semi-structured interview around the question “what was TAE like as a creative experience?”. It was analyzed by creating evocative narrative accounts of each interview and sensing into my own embodied response to the data to create emergent themes that try to be evocative as well as conceptually precise.

Beyond the DEI Checkbox: Decolonizing Professionalism and Supporting First-Generation Therapists - An Interview with Adriana Rodriguez, LMFT

Adriana Rodriguez, LMFT, on DEI beyond the checkbox, decolonizing professionalism, and first-generation therapists.

Curt and Katie welcome back Adriana Rodriguez, LMFT, a Sacramento-based psychotherapist, educator, and supervisor, to talk about what happens to DEI in the therapy profession once the mandates go away. Adriana is a Salvadoran immigrant and first-generation college graduate who now teaches graduate-level marriage and family therapy. She has watched the DEI conversations that filled 2020 and 2021 go quiet in trainings, classrooms, and supervision, and she makes the case that whatever continues now shows what therapists actually embodied.

Adriana explains why decolonizing your practice starts with the self of the therapist, drawing on Harry Aponte and Bowen’s concept of differentiation. She describes how colonized ideas of professionalism, from dress codes to agencies with no Spanish forms for their bilingual clinicians, still decide who feels like they belong in the field. She also talks about how therapists in gatekeeping roles can hold themselves accountable with compassion.

This conversation is for clinical supervisors, graduate educators, first-generation and bilingual therapists, and any therapist who wants DEI and cultural humility to show up in how they practice, supervise, and hire.

In this episode, we discuss:

- Why a DEI training is the starting point for changing how you supervise, hire, and compensate

- How self-of-the-therapist work and Bowen’s differentiation help therapists stay with hard conversations about privilege

- What the quieting of DEI reveals about the profession’s commitments

videos.title: Co gdyby Kraków przyjął Marię Skłodowską w 1894?
videos.description:
Latem 1894 roku Maria Skłodowska, świeżo po licencjatach z fizyki i matematyki na Sorbonie, starała się o asystenturę w katedrze fizyki Uniwersytetu Jagiellońskiego. Profesor był jej życzliwy, ale uczelnia nie przyjmowała wtedy kobiet nawet na studia, więc usłyszała odmowę i wróciła do Paryża, gdzie dziewięć lat później dostała Nobla, a po kolejnych ośmiu drugiego. Najpierw prawdziwa historia: Warszawa pod zaborem rosyjskim, tajne wykłady, paryskie poddasze, szopa przy ulicy Lhomond, polon i rad. Potem skok w inną historię: co by było, gdyby Kraków powiedział „tak”, z rudą z Jachymowa w tym samym państwie, ale bez Piotra Curie i przyrządu braci Curie?

videos.title: How to Build a Cashflow That Pays You for Life
videos.description:
If your income stops the moment you stop working, how free are you really?

In this video, we follow two hypothetical people, Maya and Daniel, who start at the same age with the same salary and make very different decisions. Their choices show the real difference between earning money with your time and building cashflow that is attached to assets.

This video lays out a practical roadmap for building durable cashflow, one step at a time:

Finding your number: how to calculate what you actually spend each month so your goal is a real target instead of a vague idea of financial freedom
Building a foundation: why high-interest debt and an emergency cash reserve come before investing
Creating the gap: how to invest the difference between what you earn and what you spend, and why automating it protects you from willpower and lifestyle creep
Choosing income sources: how investments (dividends and bonds), property (rental income), and businesses (content and digital products) each carry different risks, costs, and time commitments
Reinvesting and compounding: why the early years feel slow, and why patience is a financial strategy
Diversifying and protecting: spreading income across sources and watching fees, taxes, and inflation

Along the way, the video explains the four percent rule as a historical withdrawal guideline and starting estimate, not a guarantee. It also covers why a portfolio's sustainable withdrawals are not the same thing as the income it pays out, and why a realistic target should leave room for taxes, healthcare, surprise expenses, and rising prices.

Many videos on passive income skip the unglamorous parts. This one looks at the trade-offs: passive income is rarely passive at the start, every income source has a price, and the best choice is the one you can actually stick with.

This video is for anyone who wants to understand how cashflow, assets, and long-term investing work. It's especially useful for investing beginners, people interested in personal finance, aspiring entrepreneurs, long-term investors, and anyone working toward financial independence or trying to build wealth.

videos.title: 21 dni na zmianę nawyku? Co naprawdę zauważył chirurg Maxwell Maltz
videos.description:
Czy naprawdę wystarczy 21 dni, żeby zmienić nawyk? W tym odcinku sprawdzamy, skąd wzięła się ta słynna liczba. Okazuje się, że nie wymyślił jej coach, tylko nowojorski chirurg plastyczny Maxwell Maltz, autor książki „Psychocybernetyka” z 1960 roku.

Dowiesz się, co Maltz naprawdę napisał o dwudziestu jeden dniach i jakie trzy drobne słowa zgubiły się, kiedy jego zdanie krążyło po świecie. Poznasz jego pojęcie obrazu siebie i jego zdanie o wewnętrznych bliznach. Zobaczysz też, na czym polega ćwiczenie teatru umysłu, które zalecał wykonywać codziennie w ciszy. Na końcu zapiszesz swój nowy obraz siebie w pięciu linijkach.

Jeśli kiedyś skreślałaś 21 kratek, a dwudziestego drugiego dnia wszystko wróciło do starego, ten film może przynieść ci ulgę. To nie twoja wina, tylko skutek hasła, którego autor nigdy nie napisał. Zostań do końca, bo Maltz miał zaskakująco łagodną odpowiedź na pytanie, co zrobić, gdy stare przyzwyczajenie wraca.

Liczba „21 dni” nie wzięła się z badań nad nawykami. Narodziła się w gabinecie chirurga plastycznego, który patrzył, jak pacjenci przyzwyczajają się do nowej twarzy. W tym odcinku czytamy, co Maxwell Maltz naprawdę napisał w 1960 roku, poznajemy jego „teatr umysłu” i zapisujemy w zeszycie nowy obraz siebie w pięciu linijkach.
Dziennik intencji: czego uczyli mistrzowie, technika po technice. Jedna technika w każdym odcinku, do zrobienia w zeszycie.

videos.title: How Government Borrowing Affects the Economy: Budget Deficits and Interest Rates Explained
videos.description:
How Government Borrowing Affects the Economy: Budget Deficits, Interest Rates & Crowding Out Explained

Government borrowing never happens in a vacuum. In this economics explained video, we break down how budget deficits, interest rates, trade, and private investment are all connected through the national saving and investment identity.

This video covers Chapter 18—The Impacts of Government Borrowing—from the free OpenStax Macroeconomics textbook.

What happens to the rest of the economy when the government spends more than it collects? When public debt climbs, the money has to come from somewhere—and the ripple effects touch everything from interest rates and the value of the dollar to private business investment and college tuition.

In this macroeconomics lesson, you'll discover the real impacts of government borrowing through the lens of the national saving and investment identity. Using the intuitive model of a balancing seesaw, we explore how budget deficits must be offset by shifts in private saving, reductions in business investment, or increases in the trade deficit. You'll learn why budget deficits and trade deficits are often called "cousins rather than twins," how rising interest rates draw in foreign capital to strengthen the dollar, and why heavy reliance on short-term foreign borrowing can trigger severe currency and banking crises.

We also examine foundational economic theories like Ricardian equivalence and the crowding out effect, analyzing how public borrowing competes with private capital formation. Finally, we look at the crucial difference between debt used for immediate consumption versus long-term investments in physical infrastructure, human capital, and technology.

⭐ In This Video, You'll Learn: • How the national saving and investment identity balances financial capital markets • Why budget deficits and trade deficits are economic cousins rather than exact twins • How government borrowing affects interest rates and foreign exchange rates • Why short-term foreign capital inflows can increase the risk of financial crises • What Ricardian equivalence predicts about consumer saving behavior versus real-world data • How crowding out reduces private business investment in new capital equipment • The role of public investment in physical capital, human capital, and technology

An oil shock in the Strait of Hormuz. A Supreme Court ruling on tariffs. $700 billion poured into AI. Global debt heading towards 100% of world GDP. In this documentary we explain – simply, and with sources – how the world economy really works, what the United States, China, Europe and Russia each do well and badly, and where it could all lead.

videos.title: Trauma, Chronic Pain and EMDR: Exploring the Connections | Peter Bryant-Cooke
videos.description:
In this interview, I speak with psychotherapist and doctoral researcher Peter Bryant-Cooke about his work exploring EMDR and chronic pain. Peter is an accredited psychotherapist, executive coach, clinical supervisor and doctoral researcher at the University of Chester. His doctoral research explores EMDR therapy for chronic pain, bringing together clinical practice and academic enquiry.

In this episode, Peter discusses the clinical experiences that led him towards this research and the questions he hopes his PhD will help address. We explore his perspective on the relationship between trauma, distress and physical experiences, alongside the importance of listening to people whose symptoms have been difficult to explain. The conversation also considers what counts as evidence in psychotherapy and how research can account for the complexity clinicians encounter in practice.

At the time of recording, Peter was reviewing EMDR protocols used in pain research and developing plans for a later study. He describes both his ambitions for that work and the challenges of balancing doctoral research with clinical practice. For Power & Resistance, the interview raises questions about whose experiences are recognised, how knowledge shapes access to care, and how research might help services respond to people’s needs.

What would it mean for healthcare to listen more closely to patients’ experiences?

The interview discusses Peter’s views and research in progress. It is general information, not individual medical advice, and should not be read as a promise of treatment benefit.
